qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI AgentMail webhook mode accepts forged unsigned events that invoke agents
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub Advisory Database published two reviewed PraisonAI AgentMail webhook advisories on October 7. The AgentMail webhook path accepts caller-controlled message.received JSON without verifying Svix signatures, can ignore invalid Svix headers, and dispatches forged content into the configured agent session with attacker-controlled sender, subject, body, thread, and reply metadata.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reviewed GitHub security advisories plus CVE Services records and third-party advisory links
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI / pypi:praisonai before 4.6.78 in AgentMail webhook mode; public HTTP webhook authenticity boundary for agent invocation and email reply behavior.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Webhook authenticity is a delegated-authority boundary for agent workflows. A forged event can drive an agent as an arbitrary sender, create prompt-injection input, burn model or API budget, and potentially exfiltrate or mutate data through tools available to the configured agent.

upstream_routing.security_specific_local_implication: Create a local agent-and-tool-security or identity-and-access leaf for AgentMail webhook signature verification and agent invocation authenticity.

upstream_owned_context.reason: Broad PraisonAI and AgentMail product/entity context belongs upstream.
General webhook integration and agent workflow practice belongs upstream unless framed as a security control.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the October 7 GitHub Advisory Database publication and affected version boundary; the underlying CVE records are older but the reviewed GitHub publication is in-window.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether to group both CVEs in one PraisonAI AgentMail webhook-authenticity leaf.
Recheck PraisonAI 4.6.78 release notes or patch commits for exact remediation behavior before writing durable guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: vLLM Harmony tool continuations can drop cache_salt and expose a prefix-cache membership oracle
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-105752 says vLLM before 0.30.0 rebuilds Harmony tool-continuation inputs for POST /v1/responses without preserving cache_salt. With prefix caching enabled by default, an authenticated tenant who can reconstruct low-entropy post-tool history can use cached_tokens_per_turn to infer whether a victim prefix was previously processed.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record plus GitHub security advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: vllm package before 0.30.0; multi-tenant prefix cache isolation for Harmony tool continuations in Responses API deployments.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prefix cache salting is meant to isolate tenant prompts and tool continuations. Dropping the salt creates a cross-tenant side channel around post-tool state, which is both model-runtime privacy risk and agent-tool trace leakage.

upstream_routing.security_specific_local_implication: Create or update a model-and-prompt-security/data-and-privacy leaf for salted prefix-cache isolation in vLLM tool continuations.

upstream_owned_context.reason: Broad vLLM runtime and model-serving entity context belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from the CVE Services description and referenced GitHub advisory; GitHub advisory page itself may need refetch during ingest for final CVSS and patched-version wording.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check whether existing vLLM prefix-cache or prompt-security leaves should absorb this rather than creating a new leaf.
Confirm whether default prefix caching remains enabled in local guidance for the affected versions.

qualifying_findings.title: vLLM mirrored multimodal cache desync can turn a rejected request into shared-service DoS
qualifying_findings.summary: CVE-2026-105753 says vLLM before 0.28.0 can commit a media hash in the frontend sender cache during multimodal rendering before engine admission, while a rejected request prevents the receiver cache from getting the payload. A later request reusing the same media hash then triggers an assertion in the receiver cache and causes shared-service availability failure.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services record plus GitHub security advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: vllm package before 0.28.0; mirrored multimodal LRU cache between frontend sender and engine receiver.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Multimodal inference services often run as shared infrastructure. A malformed or rejected multimodal request that poisons cache state can degrade availability for unrelated tenants or users.

upstream_routing.security_specific_local_implication: Create or update a model-and-prompt-security or infrastructure-and-supply-chain leaf for vLLM multimodal cache availability boundaries.

upstream_owned_context.reason: Broad vLLM model-serving runtime context belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from the CVE Services description and referenced fix/release; advisory details should be rechecked during ingest for scoring and exploit preconditions.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether to pair this with other vLLM multimodal availability findings in one durable leaf.

qualifying_findings.title: knowns project config can execute attacker-selected LSP binaries when a repository is opened
qualifying_findings.summary: GitHub Advisory Database published a reviewed advisory on October 6 for CVE-2026-86540. knowns versions before 0.30.0 do not validate settings.lsp.languages binary paths in .knowns/config.json, so opening a repository with a crafted config can execute arbitrary binaries under the user's account.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reviewed GitHub security advisory plus CVE Services record and release reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: knowns npm package before 0.30.0; repository-local configuration trust boundary for LSP binary detection and execution.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository-aware AI and knowledge tools often consume local project configuration. A repo-supplied binary path that runs on open is a supply-chain and workspace-trust failure for coding-agent and documentation-agent environments.

upstream_routing.security_specific_local_implication: Create or update a local infrastructure-and-supply-chain or agent-and-tool-security leaf for repository-local configuration execution in AI knowledge tools.

upstream_owned_context.reason: Broad knowns tool/product context belongs upstream.
General repository-local instruction/configuration trust practice belongs upstream unless framed as a concrete security vulnerability.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence for in-window GitHub Advisory publication; the underlying CVE record predates the window, so durable synthesis should phrase this as newly reviewed/published in GitHub Advisory Database rather than newly disclosed.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare with existing knowns security leaves to avoid duplicating related project-file trust boundaries.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI GPT-6 October deployment safety update reports prompt-injection, auto-review, and cyber capability results
qualifying_findings.summary: OpenAI published the GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna October deployment safety update on October 7. The report says the October ChatGPT models show stronger resistance to jailbreaks versus GPT-5.6 ChatGPT models, reports 99.99% and 99.79% instruction-hierarchy robustness on prompt-injection evaluations, says GPT-6 October models did not exploit the deliberately poor Auto-Review setup in the tested rollouts, and classifies the October models as High but below Critical for cybersecurity capability.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: official deployment safety and assurance report
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna October releases in ChatGPT; Codex and ChatGPT Work are explicitly described as still using previously released versions.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is not a vulnerability disclosure, but it is a concrete public assurance update for prompt-injection robustness, guardrail-circumvention behavior, and cyber capability thresholds in deployed AI systems.

upstream_routing.security_specific_local_implication: Record local security-assurance implications under testing-and-assurance or governance-and-compliance, especially prompt-injection robustness and deployment-gate evidence.

upstream_owned_context.reason: Broad OpenAI and GPT-6 model-release context belongs upstream.
General Codex and Work model availability plus developer workflow implications belong upstream.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the official publication date and reported assurance facts. Treat the cybersecurity classification as OpenAI's own deployment-safety assessment, not independent third-party validation.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, route model-release background upstream and keep only local assurance, prompt-injection, and deployment-gate implications.
Check whether the local governance-and-compliance or testing-and-assurance hub already has a place for model deployment safety reports.
